verses.1: And after five days the high priest Ananias came down with some elders and an orator named Tertullus, and they laid charges against Paul before the governor.
verses.2: And when Paul had been called, Tertullus began to accuse him, saying, "Since through you we enjoy much peace, and since by your foresight reforms are being made for this nation,
verses.3: in every way and everywhere we accept this, most excellent Felix, with all gratitude.
verses.4: But, not to take up too much of your time, I beg you in your kindness to hear us briefly.
verses.5: For we have found this man to be a plague, one who stirs up riots among all the Jews throughout the world and is a ringleader of the sect of the Nazarenes.
verses.6: He even tried to desecrate the temple, and we seized him.
verses.7: And we would have judged him according to our law, but the chief captain Lysias came and with great force took him out of our hands, commanding his accusers to come before you.
verses.8: By examining him yourself you will be able to find out from him about everything of which we accuse him."
verses.9: The Jews also joined in the charge, affirming that all these things were so.
verses.10: And when the governor had motioned for him to speak, Paul answered, "Knowing that for many years you have been a judge over this nation, I cheerfully make my defense.
verses.11: You can verify that it is not more than twelve days since I went up to worship in Jerusalem,
verses.12: and they did not find me disputing with anyone or stirring up a crowd, either in the temple or in the synagogues or in the city.
verses.13: Neither can they prove to you the things of which they now accuse me.
verses.14: But this I confess to you, that according to the Way, which they call a sect, I worship the God of our fathers, believing everything laid down by the law and written in the prophets,
verses.15: having a hope in God, which these men themselves also accept, that there will be a resurrection of both the just and the unjust.
verses.16: So I always strive to have a clear conscience before God and men.
verses.17: Now after several years I came to bring alms to my nation and to present offerings.
verses.18: While I was doing this, they found me purified in the temple, without any crowd or uproar. But some Jews from Asia —
verses.19: who ought to be here before you and to make an accusation, if they have anything against me.
verses.20: Or else let these men themselves say what wrongdoing they found when I stood before the council,
verses.21: other than this one statement that I cried out while standing among them: 'It is with respect to the resurrection of the dead that I am on trial before you today.'"
verses.22: But Felix, having a rather accurate knowledge of the Way, put them off, saying, "When Lysias the commanding officer comes down, I will decide your case."
verses.23: And he ordered the centurion to keep Paul in custody but to give him some freedom, and not to prevent any of his friends from attending to his needs.
verses.24: After some days Felix came with his wife Drusilla, who was Jewish, and he sent for Paul and heard him speak about faith in Christ Jesus.
verses.25: And as Paul reasoned about righteousness and self-control and the coming judgment, Felix became alarmed and said, "Go away for now. When I find an opportunity I will summon you."
verses.26: He also hoped that money would be offered him by Paul, so he sent for him frequently and conversed with him.
verses.27: When two years had passed, Felix was succeeded by Porcius Festus. And wanting to do the Jews a favor, Felix left Paul in prison.
